tldr:
The context window is a **budget**. Everything in the request counts: system prompt, every message including tool results, tool definitions, and the output. And **more isn't better**: accuracy and recall degrade as it grows (the docs call this “context rot”). Four habits keep it under control:

- **The API is stateless.** Send the whole conversation every time (TS 5.1).
- **Keep bulk out of the main window.** Verbose exploration goes to a **subagent**, which returns a summary (TS 5.4).
- **When it fills, compact; don't clear.** Put rules that must survive in **CLAUDE.md**, because early instructions can be lost in compaction (docs).
- **Feed limited agents structured facts.** Upstream agents send key facts, citations and relevance, not reasoning chains (TS 5.1).
mentalModel: The context window is a desk, not a filing cabinet. The model sees only what's on the desk right now, and you have to put it there every time. A cluttered desk hides the important page. Clear it by filing summaries, not by sweeping everything onto the floor. Pin the house rules to the wall (CLAUDE.md) so tidying the desk never removes them.
whatItIs:
**In the guide.** TS 5.1 (pp.19–20) covers full history, tool-result growth and structured upstream output. TS 5.4
(pp.21–22) covers degradation, subagent isolation and /compact. The docs add what counts toward the window, overflow
behaviour, compaction and context editing.

**Sub-concepts — each with its picture to remember**

| # | Sub-concept | 🧭 Mental model | Reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Stateless API: send the whole history | The model has no memory between calls; the desk is cleared after every request. | ⭐ TS 5.1 · Knowledge 4 |
| 2 | Everything counts toward the window | Tools, system prompt, tool results and output all take desk space. | 📘 docs (context windows) |
| 3 | More context ≠ better (context rot) | A cluttered desk hides the important page. | 📘 docs; ⭐ TS 5.4 · Knowledge 1 |
| 4 | Explore in a subagent | Send an assistant to the library; they bring back one page of notes. | ⭐ TS 5.4 · Knowledge 3, Skill 1 |
| 5 | /compact, not /clear | File a summary of the desk; don't sweep it onto the floor. | ⭐ TS 5.4 · Skill 5 |
| 6 | Persistent rules in CLAUDE.md | House rules pinned to the wall survive every tidy-up. | 📘 docs (How Claude Code works) |
| 7 | Structured upstream output | Hand a busy colleague a one-page brief, not your notebook. | ⭐ TS 5.1 · Skill 6 |
| 8 | Overflow behaviour | Too much input → 400 “prompt is too long”; output hits the limit → model_context_window_exceeded. | 📘 docs |

**What fills the window, and what to do about it**

| # | What fills it | Symptom | Do this |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Earlier turns (needed) | — | Keep sending them. Compact when long. |
| 2 | Bulky tool results | Early details crowded out | Trim tool output (D4.7), or clear old tool results (docs: context editing, beta) |
| 3 | Exploration reads | 400 “prompt is too long” / vague answers | A subagent explores in its own window |
| 4 | Upstream reasoning chains | Later inputs dropped downstream | Structured facts + citations |
| 5 | A very long session | Degradation (TS 5.4 K1) | /compact with a focus; persistent rules in CLAUDE.md |

**Compact vs clear vs fresh start** (Claude Code)

| # | Option | Keeps | Loses | Use when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | /compact (with a focus) | Requests, key code and findings (summarised) | Detailed early instructions (docs) | The context is full mid-task |
| 2 | /clear | CLAUDE.md only | The whole conversation | Switching to an unrelated task |
| 3 | New session + structured summary | What you put in the summary | Stale tool results | Earlier results are outdated (D1.4, TS 1.7) |
howItWorks:
1. **Every API call:** send the full conversation (system prompt, tools, all turns so far). Nothing is remembered between calls.
2. **Big exploration:** hand it to a subagent. Its reads stay in its own window, and only a summary returns.
3. **Long session filling up:** `/compact` with a focus. Anything that must hold for the whole session lives in CLAUDE.md.
4. **Agent-to-agent:** upstream agents return structured key facts, citations and relevance scores that fit the downstream
   budget.
whereSeen:
- **Scenario 1 — Customer Support Resolution Agent** (Guide §5, p.3): multi-turn conversations over a stateless API.
- **Scenario 3 — Multi-Agent Research System** (Guide §5, p.4): upstream agents feeding a synthesis or report agent.
- **Scenario 4 — Developer Productivity with Claude** (Guide §5, p.4) and **Scenario 2 — Code Generation** (p.3): long
  exploration sessions, subagents, /compact.

grounding.text: If the input alone exceeds the context window, the API returns a 400 invalid_request_error (“prompt is too long”); if generation reaches the limit on newer models, the stop reason is model_context_window_exceeded.
For conversations that regularly approach the limit, server-side compaction summarises earlier turns; context editing can clear old tool results (beta).

variants.label: ✅ ⭐ full history · explore in a subagent · CLAUDE.md + /compact · structured upstream
variants.code:
from utils.ctxwin_lab import (SCENARIO, CHAT_TURNS, FILES, QUESTION, analyses, answer, chat, read, report,
                               session, spawn_explorer)   # SIMULATED context window

if SCENARIO == "stateless_history":
    history = []
    for user_msg in CHAT_TURNS:
        history.append({"role": "user", "content": user_msg})
        reply = chat(history)                    # the API is stateless: send the WHOLE conversation every time
        history.append({"role": "assistant", "content": reply})

elif SCENARIO == "exploration":
    summary = spawn_explorer(QUESTION)           # 30 files of reading happen in the subagent's own window

elif SCENARIO == "long_session":
    s = session(claude_md=["Never edit files under migrations/"])   # persistent rule: reloaded every time
    s.work(until_percent=95)
    s.compact(focus="the webhook retry change and what we found")   # summarise, keep the task and findings
    s.work_more()

else:  # downstream_budget
    results = [run(structured=True) for run in analyses()]   # key facts + citations + relevance, not reasoning chains
    report(results)
variants.observe: stateless_history: calls carry 1, 3 and 5 messages; the third reply refunds the blender on ORD-4410. exploration: the subagent reads 5 files in its own window; the main context stays at 1,800 tokens. long_session: at 95% the session compacts to 4,000 tokens, keeps the task and findings, and leaves migrations/ alone. downstream_budget: four structured analyses use 1,600 of 6,000 tokens.
variants.why: Each request carries what the model needs, and bulk stays out of the windows that can't afford it.

variants.label: ⭐❌ A — send only the newest message
variants.code:
from utils.ctxwin_lab import (SCENARIO, CHAT_TURNS, FILES, QUESTION, analyses, answer, chat, read, report,
                               session, spawn_explorer)   # SIMULATED context window

if SCENARIO == "stateless_history":
    history = []
    for user_msg in CHAT_TURNS:
        history.append({"role": "user", "content": user_msg})
        reply = chat([{"role": "user", "content": user_msg}])   # WRONG: "save tokens" - send only the newest message
        history.append({"role": "assistant", "content": reply})

elif SCENARIO == "exploration":
    summary = spawn_explorer(QUESTION)           # 30 files of reading happen in the subagent's own window

elif SCENARIO == "long_session":
    s = session(claude_md=["Never edit files under migrations/"])   # persistent rule: reloaded every time
    s.work(until_percent=95)
    s.compact(focus="the webhook retry change and what we found")   # summarise, keep the task and findings
    s.work_more()

    results = [run(structured=True) for run in analyses()]   # key facts + citations + relevance, not reasoning chains
    report(results)
variants.observe: Every call carries 1 message; by the third, the model asks again for the order number and item.
variants.why: The API is stateless: each request is all the model sees, so earlier turns must be sent again.
variants.fix: Send the whole conversation (compact it when it grows).

variants.why: Verbose exploration output fills the main window. A subagent explores in its own window and returns a summary.
variants.fix: Delegate the exploration to a subagent.

variants.label: ⭐❌ C — /clear when the context fills
variants.code:

                               session, spawn_explorer)   # SIMULATED context window

if SCENARIO == "stateless_history":

    for user_msg in CHAT_TURNS:
        history.append({"role": "user", "content": user_msg})
        reply = chat(history)                    # the API is stateless: send the WHOLE conversation every time
        history.append({"role": "assistant", "content": reply})

elif SCENARIO == "exploration":
    summary = spawn_explorer(QUESTION)           # 30 files of reading happen in the subagent's own window

elif SCENARIO == "long_session":
    s = session(claude_md=["Never edit files under migrations/"])   # persistent rule: reloaded every time

variants.observe: After /clear the agent knows neither the task nor the findings, and asks what to work on.
variants.why: /clear starts from nothing. /compact summarises and keeps the requests and key findings.

questions.q: To save tokens, a support chat built on the Messages API sends only the last three messages with each request. Customers complain that the agent asks again for order numbers they gave a few minutes earlier; this happens in 35% of chats longer than five turns. What is the right design?
opts: Keep the last three messages, but add “remember earlier details” to the system prompt.
Send the full history with every request; when it grows long, compact it rather than drop turns.
Keep the last six messages instead of three, so that most of the order numbers stay inside the window.
Send only the customer's messages, without the agent's replies, so twice as many turns fit.
questions.explain: The API is stateless, so every request needs the whole conversation. When it grows long, compact it instead of dropping turns. A asks the model to remember what it was never sent. C moves the cut-off. D breaks the conversation's structure and drops the agent's own commitments.

questions.q: An onboarding agent answering “how does billing work?” reads file after file of a 5,000-file legacy repository into its main conversation. After about 40 files, requests start failing with “prompt is too long”. What is the best redesign?
opts: Delegate the exploration to a subagent that reads in its own context and returns a summary.
Move the main agent to a model with a larger context window, so that all the files fit at once.
Read only the first 50 lines of each file, so that each one takes less of the main context.
Clear the conversation every 30 files, and continue reading from wherever the agent stopped.
questions.explain: Subagents isolate verbose exploration output and return summaries, while the main agent keeps the high-level picture. B postpones the overflow. C loses whatever sits below line 50. D throws away what was learned every 30 files.

questions.q: Two hours into a refactor in Claude Code, the context is 95% full of search output, and answers are getting generic: Claude now mentions “the usual service pattern” instead of the classes it found. The developer wants to finish the refactor in this session. What should they do?
opts: Run /clear, then restate the whole refactor task from scratch in the fresh, empty context.
Keep going and let auto-compaction kick in on its own whenever the context finally fills up.
Run /compact with a focus on the refactor, so the task and findings carry on in less context.
Start a second session for the rest of the refactor, and copy the latest diff and notes across to it.
questions.explain: /compact, with a focus, reduces context use during long exploration while keeping the task and findings. A discards the findings. B lets quality keep degrading until something forces compaction. D loses the session's understanding and keeps only its diff.

questions.q: A report agent can fit about 6,000 tokens of input. Four document-analysis subagents each send it roughly 3,000 tokens of reasoning, quotes and caveats, and the last two analyses are missing from 9 of 10 reports. The team's first idea is to truncate each analysis to 1,500 tokens. What is the most effective change?
opts: Truncate each analysis to 1,500 tokens as proposed, so that all four fit into the input budget.
Give the report agent two passes: the first on analyses 1–2, the second on analyses 3–4.
Ask the report agent to skim the analyses and focus on the parts that look most relevant.
Have the analysis subagents return structured data: key facts, citations, relevance scores.
questions.explain: When a downstream agent has a limited budget, upstream agents should return structured data rather than reasoning. A cuts content blindly, and may cut the facts. B splits the synthesis in two. D asks the model to skim input it can't fit in the first place.

questions.q: A log-investigation agent reads entire 2,000-line log files at every step, although it only needs the lines around each error. After four steps it has used 80% of its context and misses a timeout it found in step one. What is the best fix?
opts: Tell the agent in its prompt to pay special attention to anything it found in its early steps.
Switch to a model with a larger context window, so that more full log files can fit in at once.
Summarise the whole conversation after every step, keeping only the agent's latest conclusions.
Have the tool return only the relevant lines, such as each error plus its surrounding context.
questions.explain: Trim verbose tool output to the relevant part before it accumulates in the context. A asks for attention the full logs are using up. B postpones the problem. C drops the earlier findings the agent needed.

questions.q: Early in a long Claude Code session, a developer said “never touch the generated/ folder”. Hours later, after the context was compacted, Claude edits a file in generated/ and the build breaks. According to the Claude Code docs, what prevents this?
opts: Repeating the instruction every hour, so that it is always among the most recent messages in context.
Turning auto-compaction off, so that no instruction given in the conversation can ever be lost again.
Putting persistent rules like this in CLAUDE.md, which isn't lost when the conversation is compacted.
Running /compact by hand, which keeps every user instruction and summarises only the tool output.
questions.explain: The docs note that early instructions can be lost to compaction, and that rules which must persist belong in CLAUDE.md. A relies on remembering to repeat it. B trades the problem for a full context. D describes behaviour /compact doesn't guarantee.

questions.q: A support team enables prompt caching on its 8,000-token system prompt and tool definitions, expecting to “free up context window space”. Conversations still hit the limit at the same point, around turn 60. Why?
opts: Caching takes effect only after 24 hours, so the space saving simply hasn't started yet.
Caching applies only to tool definitions, so the system prompt still takes up its full space.
Cached prefixes still occupy the window; caching changes cost and speed, not what counts.
Caching frees window space only in batch requests, not in real-time support conversations.
questions.explain: Cached content still counts toward the context window. Caching reuses processing, which changes cost and latency, not window usage. A, B and D invent restrictions.

faq.q: Isn't a bigger context window the answer?
faq.a: It raises the ceiling, but more context isn't automatically better. The docs describe accuracy and recall degrading as tokens grow. What you put in the window matters as much as its size.

faq.q: How is this different from D4.7 Attention Engineering and D5.2 Case Facts?
faq.a: D4.7 covers how to lay out a long input so the important parts get used. D5.2 covers keeping exact facts outside summaries. This page covers the window as a budget: what each request must carry, and what should never enter the main window.

faq.q: What does the API do when the window overflows?
faq.a: Per the docs: if the input alone is too big, you get a 400 “prompt is too long”. On newer models, if generation hits the limit, the stop reason is model_context_window_exceeded, which should be handled as truncated (D1.3).
The guide names /compact in Claude Code (TS 5.4 Skill 5). The API's server-side compaction and context editing are docs-only here, and marked 📘.
